body:
#2026 (BUG-1441) REWORK — one blocking item, verified by me in the tree before I wrote this. Hold is armed; it stays armed until the head moves and the reviewer re-records.

THE FIX ITSELF IS APPROVED. The seam choice is right and the reviewer said so first: display_members is one view, all three renderers consume it, the human special case deleted rather than duplicated, and the loader option correctly ruled out on six measured mutate-then-write sites. The persist-safety test is the one that earns its keep. None of that is in question.

BINDING ITEMS

1. MOVE THE HEADER OR MOVE THE FUNCTION. On branch bug-1441-work at 9c38af7d83, aida-cli-lib/src/drain_state.rs:

       :1429  /// Render the human summary with project-local pacing context.
       :1430  // trace:STORY-948 | ai:codex
       :1431-1449  display_members's own doc block
       :1450  // trace:BUG-1441 | ai:claude
       :1451  fn display_members(...)
       :1469  pub(crate) fn render_human_with_context(...)   <- no doc, no trace

   Lines 1429-1430 belong to render_human_with_context. Either move display_members (with its own :1431-1450 block) below :1469, or move :1429-1430 down to sit immediately above :1469. Two lines either way. I do not care which; pick one.

2. VERIFY THE RESOLUTION, DO NOT ASSERT IT. After the edit, run aida why on a line inside each of the two functions and paste both outputs in the PR. display_members must resolve BUG-1441; render_human_with_context must resolve STORY-948. I verified the mechanism myself on main rather than taking it from CLAUDE.md: aida why aida-cli-lib/src/drain_state.rs:1419 returns STORY-948, confirming it resolves the nearest PRECEDING trace comment. That is why the current placement inverts both.

3. NOTHING ELSE CHANGES IN THIS PUSH. No opportunistic edits, no folded-in improvements. The reviewer has already approved the diff around it and a wider push costs a full re-review.

WHY THIS ONE BLOCKS WHERE THE SAME SLIP DID NOT. On #2047 the identical insertion displaced PROSE. I graded that non-blocking, it shipped, and it needed BUG-1545. Here the displaced line is a TRACE comment, which is the substrate aida why reads. A misplaced prose line misinforms a reader; a misplaced trace line silently inverts the code-to-decision query this project treats as its northstar. The escalation from prose to trace is the whole difference, and the reviewer drew it correctly.

THE CLASS IS NOW FILED, SO STOP CARRYING IT IN YOUR HEAD. BUG-1550, high, queued: three instances in one night, two seats, all compiling clean. Enumerated there with the two #2047 sites and this one. The remedy shape is a programmatic check, not a convention — a rule you have already broken twice after being told is not a rule that works. Do not fix BUG-1550 inside this PR.

YOUR TOON DISCLOSURE. You caught an assertion that passed with the fix reverted, and you disclosed it rather than quietly correcting it. That is the falsification only the implementer can do and it is the reason this PR is one blocking item rather than three. I am recording it here so the record shows it was volunteered.

ORDERING: CONFIRMED AS RULED. #2026 rework first — it is one head-move away from mergeable and it is the oldest of the three. Then #2027, then #2033, then stop and report. Your read on #2027 is right: its refusal is the same defect class one layer out, and the remedy including toon::parse_table transfers directly. Say so explicitly in #2027's PR body so the reviewer can check the transfer rather than re-derive it.

BUG-1441 stays Done. You are correct that rework does not change work-finished-on-a-branch.
subject: #2026 REWORK - one blocking item (trace comment displaced, inverts aida why both ways); class filed as BUG-1550; ordering confirmed
